## Points and plus-minus can't show who plays well *together*

- Results also depend on teammates, opponents and minutes played
- Individual stats say who is good, not which combinations work

::: {.callout-note}
## Question
Which LTU pairings create more value than their individual ratings would predict?
:::

::: notes
(45 sec) Hook: a player can look good only because of who is beside her. Say the question aloud and keep it as the thread of the talk.
:::

## Data: 10 LTU games, 8 usable

- UBL women's 2025 play-by-play: substitutions, shots, game clock, player IDs (UniSport / Sportradar feed)
- 2 of 10 games dropped: lineup tracking failed when a starter had no logged action before the first substitution
- Final scores for all 61 league games, used only for the league context at the end

::: notes
(45 sec) Say clearly that play-by-play is LTU's games only. The other teams appear as opponents.
:::

## From raw events to a pair connection score

```{r}
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 2.8
#| out-width: "100%"
steps <- data.frame(
  id = 1:5,
  title = c("Lineups", "Stints", "RAPM", "Pair score", "Stability"),
  line1 = c("Reconstruct", "Same-lineup", "Ridge model", "Actual minus", "Leave one game"),
  line2 = c("on-court five", "intervals", "per stint", "predicted", "out, rescore"),
  group = c(rep("Data preparation", 2), rep("Modelling and validation", 3))
)
box_w <- 1.6; gap <- 0.5
steps$xmin <- (steps$id - 1) * (box_w + gap)
steps$xmax <- steps$xmin + box_w
steps$xmid <- (steps$xmin + steps$xmax) / 2
arrows <- data.frame(x = steps$xmax[1:4] + 0.05, xend = steps$xmin[2:5] - 0.05, y = 1, yend = 1)
ggplot() +
  geom_rect(data = steps, aes(xmin = xmin, xmax = xmax, ymin = 0, ymax = 2, fill = group)) +
  geom_text(data = steps, aes(x = xmid, y = 1.5, label = title), colour = "white", fontface = "bold", size = 7) +
  geom_text(data = steps, aes(x = xmid, y = 1.0, label = line1), colour = "white", size = 5) +
  geom_text(data = steps, aes(x = xmid, y = 0.65, label = line2), colour = "white", size = 5) +
  geom_segment(data = arrows, aes(x = x, xend = xend, y = y, yend = yend),
               arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.2, "cm"), type = "closed"), colour = "grey40") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Data preparation" = teal, "Modelling and validation" = orange), name = NULL) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(-0.1, 10.1), ylim = c(-0.1, 2.1)) +
  theme_void(base_size = 16) + theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

$$y_s=\beta_0+\sum_p \beta_p x_{sp}+\sum_o \delta_o z_{so}+\varepsilon_s \qquad C_{ij}=\frac{\sum_{s\ni i,j} d_s\,(y_s-\hat y_s)}{\sum_{s\ni i,j} d_s}$$

::: {.smaller}
$y_s$: net points per minute in stint $s$; $x_{sp}=1$ if player $p$ is on court; $z_{so}$: opponent team; $d_s$: stint length. Ridge fit, weighted by $d_s$. $C_{ij}>0$: LTU beat the full-lineup prediction while $i$ and $j$ shared the court.
:::

::: notes
(1.5 min) Walk left to right, one sentence per box. Then the equation: the pair score is just the average prediction error over stints where both players were on court. Per minute, not per possession.
:::

## Some pairs outperform what their lineups predict

```{r}
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 5.4
#| out-width: "100%"
plot_df <- bind_rows(
  slice_max(pairs, connection_score, n = 5, with_ties = FALSE),
  slice_min(pairs, connection_score, n = 5, with_ties = FALSE)
) |>
  mutate(label = sprintf("%s + %s\n%.0f min, %d games", player_1, player_2, minutes_together, n_games_together),
         label = reorder(label, connection_score))
ggplot(plot_df, aes(connection_score, label, fill = stability)) +
  geom_col() + geom_vline(xintercept = 0) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Stable positive" = teal, "Stable negative" = orange,
                               "Uncertain" = "grey60", "Insufficient stability evidence" = "grey85"),
                    name = "Leave-one-game-out") +
  labs(x = "Connection score (net points per minute above prediction)", y = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

Top and bottom 5 of 73 pairs (at least 15 minutes, 2 games). Emilia Marinkovic is in 3 of the top 5. An association, not proof of chemistry.

::: notes

:::

## Bridging is concentrated in Vitale and Hii, mostly a minutes effect

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="55%"}
```{r}
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 5.5
cent <- read.csv("LTU_centrality_player.csv") |> mutate(player_name = str_squish(player_name))
ggplot(cent, aes(weighted_betweenness, reorder(player_name, weighted_betweenness), fill = weighted_strength)) +
  geom_col() +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "grey85", high = teal, name = "Shared minutes") +
  labs(x = "Weighted betweenness", y = NULL)
```
:::
::: {.column width="45%"}
- 112 of 120 possible pairs shared the court
- All 8 gaps involve four players with only 3 to 4 games and under 53 minutes
- Minutes are spread fairly evenly (Gini 0.27), bridging is not (Gini 0.88)
:::
:::

::: notes
(1 min) Betweenness looks like tactical importance but is mostly exposure: the most-used players are the likeliest link to the rarely used ones.
:::

## LTU mostly led comfortably or played close games

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="55%"}
```{r}
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 5
ss <- read.csv("LTU_score_state_coverage.csv") |>
  mutate(share = total_minutes / sum(total_minutes),
         score_state = factor(score_state, levels = c("Leading by 6+", "Within 5 points", "Trailing by 6+")))
ggplot(ss, aes(score_state, share, fill = score_state)) +
  geom_col(show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.0f%%\n%d games", 100 * share, n_games)), vjust = -0.3, size = 6) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent, limits = c(0, 0.58)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(teal, "grey60", orange)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Share of LTU minutes")
```
:::
::: {.column width="45%"}
- Clutch window: 14 stints, 9.4 minutes, 3 games, so descriptive only
- Only 3 five-player lineups had 5+ minutes across 2+ games
:::
:::

## Do the scores generalise? Not detectably

```{r}
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 4.6
pg <- read.csv("LTU_prediction_per_game.csv") |> mutate(game = factor(row_number()))
ggplot(pg, aes(y = game)) +
  geom_segment(aes(x = rmse_baseline, xend = rmse_enhanced, yend = game), colour = "grey60") +
  geom_point(aes(x = rmse_baseline, colour = "Baseline"), size = 4) +
  geom_point(aes(x = rmse_enhanced, colour = "With pair scores"), size = 4) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("Baseline" = "grey40", "With pair scores" = orange), name = NULL) +
  labs(x = "Prediction error, weighted RMSE (lower is better)", y = "Held-out game") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

Scores fitted on 7 games, tested on the 8th: RMSE 2.30 vs 2.31, better in 4 of 8 games, permutation p = 0.34.

::: notes
(1 min) This is the honest test. The scores describe the games they came from; no evidence yet they persist. A null result with 225 stints and a noisy outcome is expected, not a failure.
:::

## Takeaways

1. Pair scores flag combinations worth a closer look, for example those involving Emilia Marinkovic
2. The rotation is broad, and the bridging role mostly follows minutes
3. Held-out testing found no evidence the scores persist, so treat them as hypotheses for coaches

::: {.smaller}
Limits: one season, 8 games, minutes rather than possessions. Next: more games and seasons.
:::

::: notes
(1 min) End broad: small-sample sports analytics needs out-of-sample checks before names are attached to effects. Then invite questions.
:::

## Stability and data quality

- Leave-one-game-out: drop a game, refit, record whether each pair stays positive (at least 80% = stable)
- Quarter-break lineups are carried over; discrepancies were flagged, not corrected

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false
# Connection score: duration-weighted mean stint residual per pair
stint_resid <- actual_net_per_minute - predicted_net_per_minute
weighted.mean(stint_resid, w = duration_sec)
```

## Centrality measures

- Strength: total shared minutes. Betweenness: lies on short paths between others (more minutes = shorter distance)
- Eigenvector: connected to well-connected players. Gini: concentration, 0 equal to 1 concentrated
